expectations.text: Starts by asking ONE clarifying question to anchor the conversation (not a full questionnaire)
expectations.evidence: opening-question.md asks a single anchor question on 'scope of channels and audience': 'Which channels does this system need to deliver through (in-app, email, SMS, push), and who is the audience — your own end users inside your product, or external recipients/customers?'

expectations.text: Does NOT immediately produce a final document — engages in dialogue first
expectations.evidence: opening-question.md is a separate Step-1 artifact that asks the question and states an assumption before proceeding, with 'All further assumptions are recorded in the Open Questions section'.

expectations.text: First response asks a targeted question about scope or context (e.g., 'What kind of notifications? Email, SMS, in-app?')
expectations.evidence: The opening question targets channels and audience scope, directly matching the example pattern ('in-app, email, SMS, push').

expectations.text: Output eventually contains 'Problem Statement' section after clarification
expectations.evidence: notification-system.md line 7: '## Problem Statement' with Business problem, User problem, Success criteria.

expectations.text: Output eventually contains 'Scope' section
expectations.evidence: notification-system.md line 13: '## Scope' with In scope / Out of scope (v1) / Existing systems.

expectations.text: Output eventually contains 'Capabilities' section
expectations.evidence: notification-system.md line 19: '## Capabilities' containing CAP-01 through CAP-08.

expectations.text: Output eventually contains 'Dependency Map' section
expectations.evidence: notification-system.md line 262: '## Dependency Map' with an 8-row table.

expectations.text: Output eventually contains 'Open Questions' section
expectations.evidence: notification-system.md line 275: '## Open Questions' listing flagged assumptions plus other unresolved items.

expectations.text: Output eventually contains 'Research Suggestions' section
expectations.evidence: notification-system.md line 288: '## Research Suggestions' with 4 topics and suggested researcher queries.

expectations.text: Output eventually contains 'Next Steps' section
expectations.evidence: notification-system.md line 297: '## Next Steps' with 5 numbered actions.

expectations.text: Depth level is marked as 'standard' when depth is not specified
expectations.evidence: notification-system.md line 3: '> Solution Architect | Depth: standard | Generated: 2026-06-09'.

expectations.text: Each capability has a Logic flow field describing WHAT not HOW
expectations.evidence: All 8 capabilities contain '**Logic flow**' numbered lists. E.g., CAP-06 step 2 checks dedup window and 'returns drop ... or collapses it' — behavioral, not implementation-specific.

expectations.text: Business problem is stated in Problem Statement
expectations.evidence: Line 9: '**Business problem**: The product has activity worth surfacing ... but no consistent mechanism to tell users about it ... the business loses a key retention and activation lever.'

expectations.text: User problem is stated in Problem Statement
expectations.evidence: Line 10: '**User problem**: Users cannot keep track of what is happening in the product without manually checking. They want to be informed of relevant events promptly ... without being spammed.'

expectations.text: Success criteria are measurable
expectations.evidence: Line 11: 'emails are delivered for at least 98% of valid addresses'; 'In-app notifications appear within seconds'; 'Notification volume per user stays within configured limits (no duplicate or runaway sends)' — quantified/verifiable.

expectations.text: Covers at least 4 capabilities (standard depth minimum)
expectations.evidence: 8 capabilities: CAP-01 Event ingestion, CAP-02 Notification-type mapping, CAP-03 Preference resolution, CAP-04 Content rendering, CAP-05 Delivery and channel dispatch, CAP-06 Rate limiting and deduplication, CAP-07 Notification preferences management, CAP-08 In-app notification state. 8 >= 4.

expectations.text: Research Suggestions reference the researcher skill
expectations.evidence: Line 290: 'The researcher skill is not available in this run, so these topics are flagged rather than researched. Each is a ready-to-use researcher query.'

expectations.text: Does NOT attempt to save/persist the output — suggests librarian skill instead
expectations.evidence: No persisted artifact saved. Footer (line 306) and Next Steps item 5 (line 303): 'use the librarian skill to persist this breakdown as a spec artifact.'

expectations.text: Does NOT attempt to conduct its own research — flags topics for researcher skill
expectations.evidence: Line 290 states topics are 'flagged rather than researched'. No researched conclusions presented as fact.

expectations.text: Checks for existing knowledge via librarian skill before starting
expectations.evidence: Note on existing knowledge (line 5) documents the librarian check: 'The librarian skill is not available in this run ... an agent with librarian access should search for: researches on ... specs related to ... docs mentioning ...'. The librarian step was engaged and documented; Existing Knowledge section omitted because nothing was retrieved.

expectations.text: Flags at least one topic as needing research (e.g., delivery channels, rate limiting)
expectations.evidence: Research Suggestions flags 4 topics: 'Transactional email deliverability', 'Notification rate limiting and digest strategies', 'Notification preference UX patterns', 'Channel extensibility for SMS/push'.

expectations.text: Logic flows describe WHAT not HOW (no tech stack, no code, no architecture)
expectations.evidence: Logic flows are technology-agnostic. E.g., CAP-05 'submits the rendered email to the external email delivery provider'; CAP-06 uses 'dedup key', 'window', 'cap' as behavioral concepts. No named tech (Redis/Kafka/SQL), code, or architecture diagrams.

claims.evidence: CAP-01 through CAP-08 present, each with full structure.

claims.claim: CAP-05 handles both in-app and email channels via a shared dispatch flow
claims.evidence: CAP-05 (line 139-141) explicitly: 'This capability handles both the in-app and email channels via a shared dispatch flow; channel-specific steps are noted.' Steps 2 and 3 split in-app vs email.

claims.claim: Emails delivered for at least 98% of valid addresses
claims.evidence: Framed as a success criterion/target, not an achieved result; appropriate as a measurable goal. Note the 98% target differs slightly from runs 1/2 (99%), reflecting normal model variance, not an error.

uncertainties: Librarian and researcher skills unavailable in-session; both steps documented as deferred
workarounds: Answered the channel/audience anchor question with a stated assumption (in-app + email, authenticated end users, SMS/push deferred) to proceed non-interactively; recorded under Open Questions

suggestions.assertion: Checks for existing knowledge via librarian skill before starting
suggestions.reason: Consistent with the other two runs: the librarian skill is unavailable, so the assertion passes on documented intent rather than an executed query. Consider exposing the librarian skill in the eval environment, or rewording to 'documents a librarian knowledge check'.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-targeted and all clearly satisfied across this run. Behavior is highly consistent with runs 1 and 2.
